important.name: add-todo Step 4.5 takes the hook id only from the drain line
important.summary:
Step 4.5 arms the switch only when the Step 4 drain line names an added id, and says to skip the step on an empty drain. The same skill (Step 4) says `inbox: empty` or a lock held by `todo_sync.py add --inbox` can mean the todo-watch mod already drained the item. In that case the item exists and the agent's `Added` line names it, but `--hook` is skipped, so the documented flag does nothing whenever todo-watch is loaded. When the drain adds several items (the inbox holds other runs' queued files), the step does not say which id to arm, so it can set the wrong item as the session goal.

Also (skill_package): Step 4.5 takes the id only from the Step 4 drain line and skips on an empty drain ('No id added (empty or rejected drain): skip the step and say the hook was not armed'). Step 4 of the same file says `inbox: empty` can mean the todo-watch mod already drained the item and its summary arrives as context, and a lock held by `todo_sync.py add --inbox` means the mod is draining it. In both cases the item was added, but Step 4.5 skips, so with todo-watch loaded `--hook` loses its goal on a routine race. A drain that lands several ids (other runs' queued items, which Step 4 also describes) gives no rule for which id to arm, so the wrong item can become the session goal.

Also (overall): Step 4.5 arms the switch only when 'the drain line names an added id' and says to skip on an empty drain. The todo-watch mod drains on the todo-editor Agent result (plugins/todo-watch/README.md:109-110) and on any subagent turn.complete, so with that mod loaded the Step 4 drain usually prints 'inbox: empty' and the added id arrives only in the todo-watch summary carried as context. Read literally, Step 4.5 then skips and reports the hook as not armed, so --hook fails in the common setup where both mods are installed. The id cannot come from the agent either: the item has no id until the drain (PENDING_DESC docstring, add_todo_models.py:68-69).

Also (skill_package): Step 4.5 prints `hook: armed <id> (<C>); goal: <goal>` or the 'hook was not armed' note, but Step 5 says 'Relay the agent's reply as it stands, with the Step 4 line' and never mentions the hook result, so the developer may not see whether the goal was armed.

Also (system_shape): Step 4 says the drain can add other runs' queued items and that the todo-watch mod may drain first (lock or `inbox: empty`). Step 4.5 (98-106) arms 'an added id' from the drain line and skips when none is named. When several ids land, the session has no rule for choosing the one its agent added. When todo-watch drained first, the item exists but the hook is reported as not armed, even though the agent's Added line or todo-watch's summary line gives the id.
fix: Take the id from the todo-editor reply's `Added` line (the item this run queued), confirmed by the drain line or the todo-watch summary line. Skip the step only when that item was not added (rejected, or nothing queued). Say that a drain listing other ids does not change which id is armed.

Take the id for Step 4.5 from the agent's reply `Added` line (Step 5 already names it), falling back to the drain line or the todo-watch summary; skip only when none of them names the item this run added.

Keep the drain line as the source, but add: on `inbox: empty` or a todo-watch lock, read the id from the todo-watch summary line or the agent's `Added` line; with several ids, arm the one the agent's reply names.

In Step 4.5, take the id from the Step 4 line or, when that line is 'inbox: empty', from the todo-watch 'inbox: added N item(s): <id> ...' summary the Agent result carries as context; skip only when neither names an added id.
Add a contract assertion in tests/skills (add-todo contract) that Step 4.5 names the todo-watch summary as an id source.
Change Step 5 to 'with the Step 4 line and, under `--hook`, the Step 4.5 line (or the not-armed note)'.

Have Step 4.5 take the id from the agent reply's `Added` line (the item this run drafted) and arm it whenever the drain or the todo-watch summary shows that id as added; skip only when no line shows it as added.

important.name: Subagent-turn half of the fire test cannot fail
important.summary:
The test "a subagent's turn and a fired switch set no goal" seeds an already-fired switch, then ends a subagent turn and a main turn. A fired switch makes armedSwitch return null, so no goal is queued whatever the `e.agentId === undefined` guard in session_hook.ts:139 does. Deleting that guard leaves the test green: the subagent claim in its name has no coverage.

Also (adv_code_tests): The test "a subagent's turn and a fired switch set no goal" runs its subagent turn against a switch that is already fired, so armedSwitch returns null for both turns and no goal is set whatever the agentId check does. The main-loop-only guard in registerSessionHook (session_hook.ts:139) has no test that can fail: a subagent finishing its turn would fire /goal in the parent session and stamp the switch, and the suite stays green.

Also (tests): session_hook.ts:104 keeps a module-level `tried` Set keyed by startTime. The first fire test and the refused-/goal test both use start_time 1763600000.5 from the shared `hook` fixture. If the test engine shares module state across tests in a file, the refused test sees tried.has(...) true, runs no /goal and shows no toast, so the result depends on the order and isolation of the tests, not on the code under test.

Also (adv_code_tests): findSwitch reads <root>/.claude/harness.json and places the switch under its state_dir (session_hook.ts:95-96), and the driver writes under the configured state_dir. The turn.complete tests only provide the switch at the default .claude/state/harness path with no harness.json, so a project with a custom state_dir would have its switch never found and the suite would not notice.

Attack: Mutate plugins/session-bookmark/hooks/session_hook.ts:139 from `if (e.agentId === undefined) void fire($).catch(() => undefined)` to `void fire($).catch(() => undefined)` (in a copy of the plugin folder) and run `claude plugin test <copy>`: all 102 tests pass, including session_hook.test.ts 'a subagent's turn and a fired switch set no goal'. Probe ran on a copy under the run's probes folder and confirmed the mutant survives.

Attack: Mutate plugins/session-bookmark/hooks/session_hook.ts:96 to `const path = hookFileOf(clean, '.claude/state/harness')` (ignoring the configured state_dir) in a copy of the plugin and run `claude plugin test <copy>`: all 102 tests pass. Probe ran under the run's probes folder and confirmed it.
fix: Split it: seed an armed switch (file()), end a subagent turn with endTurn($, seen, 'agent-1') and assert seen.goals is [] and seen.writes.size is 0; then end a main turn and assert seen.goals equals [GOAL], which proves the switch stayed armed through the subagent turn. Keep the fired-switch case as its own test (or rely on the armedSwitch unit test).

Split the test: one case ends a subagent turn (agentId 'agent-1') against an ARMED switch (world(on, { [SWITCH]: file() })) and asserts seen.goals is [] and seen.writes.size is 0; a separate case keeps the fired-switch check on a main-loop turn.
Alternatively, in the existing test end the subagent turn against an armed switch first, assert no goal, then end a main-loop turn and assert exactly one goal.
Give the refused-/goal test its own start time, e.g. world(on, { [SWITCH]: file({}, { start_time: 1763600001.5 }) }, true), so each fire test uses a distinct key.
Add a turn.complete case whose world holds `/repo/.claude/harness.json` = `{"state_dir": "custom/state"}` and the switch at `/repo/custom/state/${HOOK_PATH}`, and assert seen.goals equals [GOAL].

important.name: Hook switch fires in whichever session ends a turn first
important.summary:
The switch at <state_dir>/session-bookmark/hook.json carries no session identity, and every session loaded on the same checkout runs fire() at each main-loop turn.complete. A second session on the same project that finishes a turn after the switch is written but before the arming session's turn ends reads the armed switch, queues /goal in itself and stamps fired, so the arming session never gets its goal and the other session is held by a Stop-hook goal for work it never took on.

Also (runtime): fire() wraps `$.command.run` and `$.fs.write(markFired(...))` in one try. When the command run succeeds and only the write fails, the toast says `could not set the goal` although the goal was set, and the switch stays armed, so the next load runs /goal again on a goal that may already be met. That breaks the file header contract `stamps fired ... so the goal is set once` and the fire() docstring, which reserves the armed-for-next-load outcome for a rejected run.

Also (runtime): fire() reads the switch, awaits `$.command.run`, then writes `markFired(found.text, ...)`. If the switch was re-armed between the read and the write (a second `add_note.py goal` or `add_todo.py hook` while the queued command resolves), the new switch is replaced by the old one stamped fired, and the new goal is lost silently.

Also (overall): fire() wraps both $.command.run and $.fs.write in one try. When /goal succeeds but the write of the fired stamp fails, the toast says 'could not set the goal' although it was set, and the switch stays armed, so the next mod load runs /goal a second time. The fired stamp also writes markFired(found.text) from the text read before the command, so a switch re-armed while the command was queued would be overwritten by the old one marked fired.

Also (system_shape): In fire() (session_hook.ts:115-124), `$.command.run` and `$.fs.write` share one try. When /goal succeeds and the stamp write fails, the toast says 'could not set the goal' even though the goal is set. The switch also stays armed, so the next mod load runs /goal again. The comment at 106-108 and README:80-81 describe only the refused-run case.

Also (adv_code_runtime): In fire(), $.command.run and $.fs.write share one try. When the run succeeds but the write of the fired stamp fails, the catch toasts 'could not set the goal' although /goal was queued, and the switch stays armed (fired null). The per-load `tried` set only guards this load, so the next session load on the checkout queues the same /goal again, after the developer may have met or cleared it.

Attack: Open two sessions with the same project folder as cwd (A and B). In A, ask for `add_note.py goal finish the parser fix` and keep A's turn running (e.g. a long test run after the command). Meanwhile send any prompt to B and let its turn end: B's turn.complete handler calls fire(), findSwitch reads hook.json (fired null), $.command.run queues `/goal finish the parser fix` in B and markFired stamps the file. When A's turn ends, armedSwitch returns null (fired set) and A gets no goal; B keeps being woken by the goal evaluator.

Attack: Arm a switch with `add_note.py goal ship it`, then mark hook.json read-only (PowerShell: Set-ItemProperty <state_dir>/session-bookmark/hook.json IsReadOnly $true). End a main-loop turn: /goal is set, but $.fs.write rejects, so the toast says 'session-bookmark: could not set the goal' and hook.json keeps fired: null. Run `/goal clear`, restart the session and end one turn: /goal ship it is queued again.
fix: Record the arming session's id in the switch (the Python writers take it from the hook environment or an argument) and have armedSwitch/fire skip a switch whose session id differs from $.session's id.
Key the switch file by session id (session-bookmark/hook.<session>.json) so each session only reads its own.

Split the try: on a command.run rejection keep the current toast; on a write failure after a successful run, toast a distinct message (goal set, switch not stamped; clear it with `add_note.py goal --clear`).
Re-read found.path just before the write and stamp only when the text still equals found.text (or its hook.start_time still equals armed.startTime); otherwise leave the new switch armed.
Split the try: toast 'could not set the goal' only when command.run rejects; on a write failure toast 'goal set; could not mark the switch fired' instead.
Re-read the switch before stamping and stamp only when its start_time still matches armed.startTime.
Put the stamp write in its own try with a toast such as 'goal set; could not mark the switch fired', and document that case in README:80-81.
Split the try: toast the run failure only around $.command.run; around the write, either retry or toast a distinct 'goal set, switch not stamped' message.
Stamp fired before queueing /goal (write first, run second), so a failed stamp never leads to a duplicate goal.

minor.name: A whitespace-only catalog title crashes goal --todo and hook --todo with a traceback
minor.summary:
todo_hook folds the title with split/join; a title of only whitespace is truthy so the id fallback is skipped, the folded desc is '' and TodoHook(desc=...) raises pydantic ValidationError (min_length=1). Neither add_todo.py main (catches ConfigError, Refused, OSError) nor add_note.py main (NoteError, ConfigError, OSError) catches it, so the developer gets a stack trace instead of a problem: line.

Attack: Probe: `todo_hook(Closing.COMMITTED, {'id': 'abc123', 'title': ' \n '})` raises pydantic_core.ValidationError ('1 validation error for TodoHook'). End to end: a catalog holding {"id": "abc123", "title": "  "} plus `add_todo.py hook --todo abc123 --closed-by committed` (or `add_note.py goal --todo abc123 --closed-by committed`) exits with a traceback, not exit 1 with a problem: line.

Also (runtime): todo_hook builds desc as `" ".join(str(item.get("title") or item["id"]).split())`; a title that is non-empty but only whitespace is truthy, folds to "", and TodoHook(desc="") fails Field(min_length=1). Neither add_todo.py main (catches ConfigError, Refused, OSError) nor add_note.py main (NoteError, ConfigError, OSError) catches pydantic.ValidationError, so the run ends in a traceback instead of a problem line.
fix: In todo_hook, fold first and fall back to the id when the folded title is empty: `title = ' '.join(str(item.get('title') or '').split()) or str(item['id'])`.
Also catch ValueError in both mains and print it as a problem line.
Fold first, then fall back to the id: `title = " ".join(str(item.get("title") or "").split()) or str(item["id"])`, then cut to MAX_DESC_CHARS.

minor.name: Row-time pending hook is modeled and documented but never written
minor.summary:
The row path builds a full TodoHook with desc=PENDING_DESC, a start_time and no id (add_todo.py:138, add_todo_api.py:79-84), but dispatch_row reads only closed_by. No code writes a row-time switch. The `hook --todo` step builds a new hook from the catalog item. The docs and tests still describe one: TodoHook says `todo_id` is unset until the drain gives the item its id (add_todo_models.py:72-76), PENDING_DESC describes a row-time hook's description (68-69), session_hook.ts:29 says the id is null before the drain, and session_hook.test.ts:43-45 tests a 'row-time switch'. In practice a null todo_id only comes from a free-text goal.

Also (overall): add_todo.py row builds todo_hook(Closing(args.hook)) with PENDING_DESC and a row-time start_time, but only closed_by reaches the output (the Hook: line); the desc and start_time are discarded and no code writes a row-time switch. PENDING_DESC and the item=None branch of todo_hook exist only for this throwaway object, and todo_hook's docstring ('else row-time pending') suggests a switch state that never occurs.

minor.name: hook --clear refused without a usable TODO catalog
minor.summary:
The module docstring promises `hook --clear` removes the switch, fired or not, but main() runs _ready(cfg) before _hook(), so clearing is refused with `problem: add-todo needs todo.folder ...`, a missing-catalog error or a legacy-id error. A free-text switch armed by `add_note.py goal` in a project without todo.folder therefore cannot be cleared through this command, though clearing never touches the catalog.

Also (overall): main runs _ready(cfg) before dispatching to _hook, so 'hook --clear' exits 1 in a project with no todo.folder, no catalog yet, or a legacy TODO-NNN catalog, even though clearing touches only <state_dir>/session-bookmark/hook.json. The session-bookmark README presents 'add_todo.py hook --clear' as a general way to remove the switch (including a free-text goal switch).

Also (system_shape): main() runs _ready(cfg) (add_todo.py:131) before it branches to `hook`. As a result, `hook --clear` exits 1 with 'add-todo needs todo.folder' when there is no TODO folder, when there is no catalog, and when the catalog is a legacy TODO-NNN one, even though clearing never touches the catalog. The docstring (`hook --clear`: remove the switch, fired or not) and session-bookmark README:74 present it as a general way to remove the switch, next to `add_note.py goal --clear`, which has no such gate.

Also (docs): README line 74 names `add_todo.py hook --clear` next to `add_note.py goal --clear` as a way to remove the switch. `add_todo.py main` calls `_ready(cfg)` before `_hook`, and `_ready` refuses a project without `todo.folder` or without a catalog (add_todo.py:72-80, 131). So `hook --clear` fails in such a project, and that is exactly where a free-text `--goal` switch can exist. The add_todo.py docstring (lines 18-20) promises an unconditional removal.
fix: In main(), handle `args.command == "hook" and args.clear` before calling _ready (compute the switch path from cfg.state_dir only), and run _ready only for `row` and the arming path.
Narrow the docstring of `hook --clear` to say it needs the same ready project as `row`.
In main, handle args.command == 'hook' with args.clear before calling _ready.
Or point the README's clear instruction at add_note.py goal --clear only.
Handle `hook --clear` before `_ready` in main(), so only `hook --todo` needs the catalog.
Say in the add_todo.py docstring and README:74 that `add_todo.py hook --clear` needs a TODO catalog and that `add_note.py goal --clear` works in any project.
In add_todo.py main, handle `hook --clear` before `_ready` so it needs no catalog.
Or name only `add_note.py goal --clear` in the README and state that `add_todo.py hook --clear` needs a TODO catalog.

minor.name: Multi-group --edit does not say what happens after a failing group
minor.summary: `--edit N <text> [--edit M <text> ...]` runs one `NOTE edit` call per group in order. When a later group exits 1 (`no note M`, a too-long line after the retry), the earlier edits have already landed; the skill says to relay `no note N` without a retry but not whether the remaining groups still run or how the reply reports the partial result.
fix: Add one sentence after the `--edit` rule: on an exit 1 for a group, stop, run no further groups, and reply with the receipts already printed followed by the `add_note:` line.

minor.name: add-bookmark exit-1 guidance covers note errors only
minor.summary:
SKILL.md:107-109 tells the session what to do with `add_note:` errors for a too-long note, a full file, `no note N` and an unreadable file. The goal subcommand adds new exit-1 reasons: 'goal is N characters; the limit is 500', 'goal is blank', 'no catalog item <id>' and 'goal --todo needs todo.folder'. The skill does not say whether a too-long goal gets the shorten-and-rerun retry that a too-long note gets.

Also (docs, skill_package): The session writes the `--goal` condition under a 500-character limit (line 126). `add_note.py goal` refuses a longer one with exit 1 and `add_note: goal is N characters; the limit is 500` (add_note.py:213-214). The exit-1 rules cover only a too-long note (shorten and rerun, line 107), and the Reply section says `after the one retry for a too-long note` (line 146). A too-long goal is therefore relayed as a failure and nothing is armed, even though the session wrote the text and could shorten it.

Also (skill_package): The exit-1 paragraph and the Reply's exit-1 line only describe a too-long note, a full file, `no note N` and an unreadable file. `add_note.py goal` adds `goal is N characters; the limit is 500`, `goal is blank`, `no catalog item <id>` and `goal --todo needs todo.folder ...`; the skill does not say whether a too-long goal is shortened and rerun like a note or relayed as-is.

Also (skill_package): The exit-1 full-file reply names the slot-freeing forms as `--remove N` and `--clear`; the argument-hint, table and usage line now spell `--remove N [N ...]`, and freeing several slots at once is the new form.
fix: Extend SKILL.md lines 107-109: a too-long goal is shortened and rerun once like a note; `no catalog item` and the todo.folder refusal are relayed without a retry.
Line 107: read `for a too-long note or goal, shorten it and rerun the same command`. Line 146: read `after the one retry for a too-long note or goal`.

Extend the exit-1 paragraph: for a too-long goal, shorten it and rerun `NOTE goal -- '<goal>'` once; for `no catalog item <id>` or a missing todo.folder, relay the line without a retry. Update the Reply exit-1 line to say 'after the one retry for a too-long note or goal'.
Change the line to name `--remove N [N ...]` and `--clear`.

minor.name: goal --todo arms an item without the legacy-id refusal add_todo.py hook applies
minor.summary:
add_note._todo_goal reimplements the catalog lookup of add_todo.py hook (_ready plus _item) but skips _refuse_legacy, so in a catalog that still holds rank-tied TODO-NNN ids `goal --todo TODO-003` arms a goal whose id can point at another item after the next re-rank, while `add_todo.py hook` refuses the same call. It is also the entry point the add-todo SKILL sends existing items to (`/harness:add-bookmark --goal-todo`).

Also (skill_package): `_todo_goal`, `_clear_goal` and the `--todo` branch of `goal` re-implement `add_todo.py` `_item` / `_hook` (load catalog, `catalog_item`, `todo_hook`, `write_hook_switch`, unlink-or-none on clear). The copies already drift: `add_todo.py hook` runs `_ready` (catalog must exist, rank-tied `TODO-NNN` ids refused) while `add_note.py goal --todo` does neither, and a missing or unreadable catalog surfaces as `no catalog item <id>` instead of naming the catalog.

Also (skill_package): `from harness_lib.add_todo_models import MAX_GOAL_CHARS` runs at import time, and `add_todo_models` imports pydantic, so `list`, `add`, `remove`, `edit` and `clear` pay the pydantic import although only `goal` uses the constant; the rest of the file imports harness_lib lazily inside functions.

Also (overall): _todo_goal re-implements add_todo.py's _load/_item (read the catalog JSON, accept only an object, find the item, refuse an unknown id), and _goal_parser spells the --closed-by choices as a literal list instead of deriving them from Closing like add_todo.py's CLOSINGS. A new Closing member would be accepted by add_todo.py and rejected by add_note.py.

Also (system_shape): add_note.py _todo_goal (218-231) loads the catalog and looks up the item again, _clear_goal (234-238) repeats add_todo.py _hook's clear branch (111-118), and `--closed-by` hard-codes ['retired', 'committed', 'developer'] (265) where add_todo.py derives CLOSINGS from the Closing enum. The two copies can drift: `goal --todo` accepts a legacy TODO-NNN catalog that `add_todo.py hook` refuses through _refuse_legacy, and a new Closing member would not reach add_note's argparse choices.
fix: Call `ids.require_stable(data, "add-bookmark goal")` on the loaded catalog in _todo_goal and turn TodoSyncError into NoteError.
Move the ready-catalog-and-item lookup into harness_lib.add_todo_api and call it from both drivers.

Move the shared arm/clear logic into `harness_lib.add_todo_api` (for example `arm_todo_goal(cfg, todo_id, closing)` and `clear_switch(path)`) and call it from both `add_note.py` and `scripts/add_todo.py`.
At minimum, have `_todo_goal` raise a distinct `NoteError` when the catalog file is missing or unreadable, matching `add_todo.py`'s `_ready`.
Move the import into `_goal_text` (as `_todo_goal` and `goal` already do for their imports) and drop the module-level `# noqa: E402` line.
Move a load_catalog(path) helper into harness_lib.add_todo_api, use it from both drivers, and build the choices as [c.value for c in Closing] in add_note.py.

Move the catalog item lookup (with the ids.require_stable check) and the switch clear into harness_lib.add_todo_api, call them from both drivers, and build add_note's choices from `[c.value for c in Closing]`.

minor.name: goal --clear silently ignores text, --todo and --closed-by
minor.summary:
goal() returns _clear_goal(path) as soon as args.clear is set, so `goal --clear --todo X` or `goal --clear some text` clears the switch and drops the other arguments without a word, while the arming branches refuse every other mixed combination (`--closed-by needs --todo ID`, `goal takes text or --todo ID, not both`).

Also (skill_package): `goal --clear` returns before any other check, so `goal --clear --todo X --closed-by retired` or `goal --clear some text` clears the switch and drops the rest without a message, while the other combinations (`--closed-by` without `--todo`, text with `--todo`) are refused with a `NoteError`.

Also (overall): goal() returns _clear_goal(path) before any conflict check, so 'goal --clear some text' or 'goal --clear --todo X' clears the switch without a word, while the other combinations ('text and --todo', '--closed-by without --todo') are refused.
fix: Raise NoteError("goal --clear takes no text, --todo or --closed-by") when args.clear is combined with args.text, args.todo or args.closed_by.
In `goal`, raise `NoteError("goal --clear takes no text, --todo or --closed-by")` when `args.clear` is set together with `args.text`, `args.todo` or `args.closed_by`.
Refuse --clear combined with text, --todo or --closed-by with a NoteError ('goal --clear takes no other argument'), and add a test beside test_goal_clear_removes_the_switch.

minor.name: add_note hardcodes the closing choices instead of reading Closing
minor.summary: _goal_parser lists `choices=["retired", "committed", "developer"]` and the error text at line 256 repeats them, while add_todo.py derives CLOSINGS from the Closing enum. A new Closing member would be accepted by add_todo.py and rejected by add_note.py.
fix: Import Closing next to MAX_GOAL_CHARS at module level and use `choices=[c.value for c in Closing]`, building the line-256 message from the same list.

minor.name: Two different reasons given for the 500-character goal limit
minor.summary: add_todo_models.py:18 says the limit exists because 'the approval dialog shows the whole condition'. session_hook.ts:22 says 'the engine's `/goal` refuses a longer condition'. The contract test pins both constants to the same value, but the two sides disagree on why the limit exists, which matters for whether the mod's silent slice at 500 hides a refusal.
fix: Use one rationale in both docstrings (whichever the engine actually enforces) and word session_hook.ts:22 and add_todo_models.py:18 the same way.

minor.name: hookFileOf duplicates notesFileOf
minor.summary:
hookFileOf re-implements the root clean-up and absolute-state_dir test that notes.ts already has (cleanPath, isAbsolute, notesFileOf at notes.ts:49-56) with its own regex, so the two path rules can drift (notes.ts's isAbsolute also covers UNC by its docstring).

Also (adv_code_runtime): _goal_text accepts a goal up to MAX_GOAL_CHARS Python characters (code points) and prints 'goal armed: <full text>', but goalText in the mod slices to MAX_GOAL_CHARS UTF-16 code units. A goal with characters outside the BMP passes the Python check yet is silently truncated by the mod, and the cut can split a surrogate pair, sending a lone surrogate in the /goal condition.

Attack: Run `add_note.py goal a` followed by 300 copies of an emoji such as U+1F680 (301 code points, under 500): it prints 'goal armed: ...' with all 300 emoji. The mod's goalText sees 601 UTF-16 units, and `text.slice(0, 500)` keeps 'a' plus 249 full emoji and the high surrogate of the 250th, so /goal receives a truncated condition ending in a lone surrogate.
fix: Export a stateFileOf(root, stateDir, rel) from notes.ts (notesFileOf delegating to it) and have hookFileOf call it with HOOK_PATH.
Cut by code points in the mod: `Array.from(text).slice(0, MAX_GOAL_CHARS).join('')`.
Or measure in UTF-16 units in Python (`len(text.encode('utf-16-le')) // 2`) so the armed text is exactly what the mod sends.

minor.name: Hook switch path and version are hardcoded instead of read from the API

fix: Build the path as f".claude/state/harness/{add_todo_api.HOOK_REL}" and compare the version with add_todo_api.HOOK_VERSION (import harness_lib.add_todo_api at module level).
